html:
On 29 September 2009 an undersea earthquake south of the Samoan islands sent a tsunami onto the south coast of Upolu, American Samoa and northern Tonga. Nearly 200 people died, most of them in Samoa.

The waves arrived within minutes and wiped out beach resorts and villages along Upolu's south coast. Many families then moved their homes inland, onto higher ground.

The disaster led to new warning sirens and drills across the region, a lesson taken up again after the Hunga Tonga eruption in 2022. It also hit the canneries in American Samoa.
